ranked_facts.concept_key: unilateral purulent discharge mixed with blood
ranked_facts.why: unilateral purulent discharge mixed with blood is more consistent with juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma

0eafbee3b502b4db4406d22f8fd5726bad7feb6a.why: selected fact F11 has sufficient candidate contrast

fact_rationales.F11: Unilateral purulent discharge mixed with blood is more typical of an infectious or inflammatory process, but can also be seen in neoplastic processes, although less likely in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
fact_rationales.F3: Nasal discharge with worsening pain is a non-specific symptom that can be seen in various conditions, including neoplastic processes, but is more commonly associated with infectious or inflammatory conditions.

ranked_facts.why: nasal discharge with worsening pain is more consistent with complications of sinusitis which could be related to juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma

why.B1.1: Unilateral purulent discharge mixed with blood and nasal discharge with worsening pain are consistent with Acute Bacterial Sinusitis
why.B2.1: Foreign body obstruction could cause unilateral purulent discharge, but the presence of worsening pain and the patient's history of previously diagnosed acute sinusitis make it less likely
why.B3.4: Allergic Rhinitis is unlikely due to the presence of purulent discharge and worsening pain, which are not typical symptoms of allergic rhinitis
why.B4.1: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma is a rare condition and the symptoms presented do not strongly suggest this diagnosis, especially given the patient's age and the presence of a previous diagnosis of acute sinusitis
